draftPackage.topic: Reading a burned scroll without physically opening it
draftPackage.centralQuestion: How can writing be read inside a scroll too fragile to open?
draftPackage.thesis: A detectable ink signal and traced internal surfaces can be mapped into readable digital images while leaving the fragile original rolled up.
draftPackage.viewerPayoff: Understand the distinction between physically opening a page and computationally locating, texturing and flattening its surviving surface.

segments.text: This burned scroll was too fragile to open. Scientists read it anyway.
The En-Gedi scroll crumbled when it was touched.
Researchers scanned it with X-rays, building a three-dimensional map.
Inside that scan, they traced the surviving layers.
In this scroll, the ink showed up more densely than the parchment.
They mapped that signal onto digital surfaces, then flattened them into readable images.
The recovered Hebrew text came from the Book of Leviticus.
This worked because the ink was detectable in the scan. Different materials need different approaches.
They revealed surviving writing without unrolling the fragile original.

misconceptionSafeguards: The actual artifact never physically unrolls in the animation.
Marks are illustrative, not Hebrew transcription or original scan data.
The method needs detectable surviving ink; no guessing or resurrection of destroyed writing.
Higher scan density is observed; ink metal identity is not established.
No Herculaneum, exact age, oldest-Bible, theological or safety claim.
review.comprehensionReview: Task has a concrete obstacle; volume leads to traced surface, contrast is carried onto that surface and flattened. Return distinguishes unchanged object from readable image. Material boundary prevents universal magic-scanner takeaway.
review.rightsReview: Original SVG geometry and illustrative marks only. Research figures have noncommercial terms and are never reused. Existing OFL Manrope and local Kokoro terms; no purchases or new paid services.

careAssessment.rationale: Technical conservation-method explanation, neutral identification of documented text. No religious/political verdict, high-care medical issue, unresolved rights or material central evidence conflict.
